claims.claim_text: The subject immediately fled southbound on foot upon seeing Officer Dahl and was observed entering the Walmart parking lot.
At approximately 1629 hours, Officer T. Ross and Officer A. Gutierrez observed the subject walking eastbound on Adams Way near Grand Avenue.

APD Sgt. J. Harmon distributed a wanted flyer identifying the subject as Renteria, who was wanted by the Buena Park Police Department in connection with a residential burglary in which a firearm was stolen.
Officers within the helicopter made repeated public address announcements in English and Spanish, directing the subject to exit the residence at 7896 Adams with his hands raised.
The subject was observed through the windows walking up and down the stairs but made no effort to comply.
I observed the subject exit from the front door of 7896 Adams.
The subject walked directly toward our position in the backyard of 7914 Adams.
There was adequate ambient lighting from nearby streetlights, and I was able to clearly see the subject's hands and movements as he approached.
The subject was carrying an object in his right hand that I believed to be a dark-colored handgun.
The subject stopped approximately 20 feet from our position, raised both hands above his head, and then suddenly lowered his right hand toward his waistband.
I discharged my firearm four times at the subject's center mass.
I observed the subject had sustained gunshot wounds to his upper torso and right arm.

A search of the immediate area revealed a black semi-automatic handgun on the ground approximately three feet from where the subject fell, consistent with the subject having dropped the weapon when he was shot.
At approximately 1615 hours, APD dispatch received a 911 call reporting a male subject brandishing a firearm at a reporting party in a vehicle.
The subject fled on foot and jumped a wall into the yard of a residence at 7944 Adams Way.
